content.title: About
content.content: The Quarter Pounder is a classic McDonald's burger featuring a 113 g (¼‑lb) beef patty, American cheese, onions, pickles, ketchup and mustard, served on a sesame‑seed bun.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The burger was introduced to the U.S. menu in 1971 and quickly became a staple.
The name reflects the patty’s weight – a quarter of a pound (≈ 113 g).
In some markets, such as Japan, a double‑patty version called the “Double Quarter Pounder” is offered.
Since the 2020s McDonald's has offered a “Quarter Pounder with Cheese” without onions and pickles upon customer request.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The beef patty provides about 20 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is readily absorbed.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc aids immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: American cheese adds calcium for bone health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of protein, fat and carbs offers a quick energy boost.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: One Quarter Pounder contains roughly 520 kcal, so it should be accounted for in daily intake.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: The patty and cheese contribute saturated fat and salt, which can affect cholesterol and blood pressure.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The sesame bun contains gluten, important for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: American cheese may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burger is served hot. It can be customized with extra sauces, added bacon, or a gluten‑free bun upon request.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burger in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze it and reheat in a microwave or oven before eating.
